::: {#exm-loop-parallel}
#### A loop and two parallel edges

The graph in @fig-loop-parallel has vertices $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$, and five edges:

- a loop (@def-graph-loop) at $p$;
- an edge joining $p$ and $q$;
- two parallel edges (@def-parallel-edges) joining $q$ and $r$;
- an edge joining $r$ and $s$.

The two edges joining $q$ and $r$ have the same set of endpoints, $\set{q, r}$,
so writing an edge as the set of its endpoints does not tell them apart.
We name them instead, say $e_1$ and $e_2$, and say that each has endpoints $q$ and $r$.

::: {#fig-loop-parallel}

![](../images/graphs-loop-parallel.png){fig-alt="Four points p, q, r and s in a row.
A small loop leaves p and comes back to p.
One line joins p and q, two curved lines join q and r, and one line joins r and s." width="60%"}

A graph with a loop at $p$ and two parallel edges between $q$ and $r$.
